utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon. I would first of all like to check that you can hear the translation of what I'm saying in your own language. If that's the case, can you please tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can indeed hear and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were called as a witness by the Defence team for General Kubura. Before asking you to take an oath, I would like to identify you. Could you give me your name, your family name, and your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm Major Kasim Podzic, and I was born on the 14th of October, 1972, at Hadzici, near Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've just said that you are a commander. Could you tell me where you are a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a member of the BH armed forces, so within the framework of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you also tell me in 1992 and 1993, at that time did you have job? If it was a military position, could you let me know what the name of the unit was, the unit that you belonged to. And if you were a commander, could you tell me in what way, what did you command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. In 1992, I had completed the military academy in the former JNA. Up until the 15th of April, 1993, I was abroad. I was in the Republic of Macedonia. On the 15th of January, 1993, I joined the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I stayed there until the 15th of March, 1993, within the first anti-sabotage unit for the defence of Zenica. And between the 15th of March, 1993, all the way until mid-January 1996, I was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Between the 15th of March, 1993, and the beginning of August 1993, I was an operations and training officer within the 2nd Battalion. And as of August 1993 until January 1996, I was a commander of the 1st or the 2nd Battalion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear. The 2nd Battalion apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before a national or international court with regard to the facts that happened in your country in 1992 or 1993, or is it the first time you testified before a court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read the text of the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may sit down. Before I give the floor to the lawyers that you have met during the proofing, I would just like to provide you with some elements of information as to the way this hearing is going to take place, as I do with regard to most witnesses in order to make sure that it all goes well. You will have to first of all answer questions put to you by General Kubura's Defence team. These questions will be called within the framework of what we call the examination-in-chief. Following the questions by the Defence team for General Kubura, General Hadzihasanovic's Defence team will also be allowed to ask any questions they feel might be appropriate. Once the Defence team will have asked all the questions, the Prosecution, sitting to your right, will also ask you questions for more or less the same period of time within the framework of what we tend to call cross-examination. After the cross-examination, General Kubura's Defence counsel will be able to ask additional questions, that is to say questions relating to the questions asked by the Prosecution. There upon, the three Judges sitting in front of you, if they feel the need, will also be able to ask you questions. And once the Judges will have asked all the questions, they will give the floor once again to both the Defence and Prosecution, and they will be able to ask any useful questions they feel they have to ask following your answers to the Judges' questions. I should also draw your attention to a number of other aspects of the situation. You have just taken an oath which means that, obviously, you must tell the truth and you can't lie, because perjury is a crime, as you know. Apart from anything else, I would also like to draw your attention to another rather complex aspect of our procedure. If we ask you a question, you're also allowed to say, I don't feel like answering that question. Why can you say that? Only in case you might be led to think that this answer might at some point be used against him and represent certain elements which may be used against him. So in that case - and this I must say has never happened so far, but it is a possibility which is provided for in our Rules of Procedure - you might nevertheless be forced to answer. But in that case, the Trial Chamber would grant you immunity. Let me also draw your attention to another point. This is an -- a basically oral procedure and this is the reason why can see the English transcript of what I'm saying on the screen in front of you, and this refers to everything else that is being said in the course of this hearing. This is why it is particularly important to try when answering these questions to be as specific as possible and as concise as possible because a question, as you know, calls for a specific answer. If you encounter any sort of difficulty, don't hesitate to let us know; that's why we're there, to solve such problems. In a little while, we shall have a short break, about 20 to 25 minutes, in order to make it possible for the tapes to be changed and also to give you some rest. The Defence has told us that, a priori, they don't think it will take too long, and it may well happen that we finish today. If we don't finish today, we will continue tomorrow morning. So these are some elements that I wanted to inform you about before I give the floor to the Defence counsel, who is going to start with the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Podzic, you have just answered some questions put to you by the Presiding Judge. You have informed us of what you did in the course of the war and after the war. But what do you do now and where are you located?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I'm currently a member of the Federation army. I am part of the peace mission in Congo, where I work as a military observer. In the post-war period I completed a number of courses. I would single out two courses, command staff courses, within NATO. There was a peacekeeping operation course and an NBI training course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: From the 25th of November of last year up until the 25th of November this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question hasn't been entered in the transcript. Since when have you had these duties and up until when will you be performing these duties?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: As a military observer -- I've been working as a military observer since the 25th of November of last year up until the 25th of November of this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, you said that up until March 1993 you were a member of the Territorial Defence in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When exactly did you join the 7th Muslim Brigade and how?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I became a member of the 7th Muslim on the 15th of March, 1993, in accordance with an order from the superior command, or rather in accordance with an order from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in the 7th Brigade, were you assigned duties of any kind and up until when did you perform your duties?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: When I joined the 7th Muslim Brigade I was appointed as an officer for operations and training within the 2nd Battalion. The duties were similar to the duties of deputy commander of the battalion. I remained in that position until the end of July or perhaps beginning of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, when answering the questions, could you answer a little more slowly to enable the interpreters to follow you. Who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: My immediate superior was the commander of the 2nd Battalion, Serif Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way was the battalion organised?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The battalion had about 400 members and it consisted of two detachments. There were two companies in each detachment. There was an accompanying company, two anti-sabotage detachments that reported directly to the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your battalion located?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: It was located in the Bilmiste barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in 7th Brigade, who was the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade was Mr. Asim Koricic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Mr. Kubura when you joined the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I also met Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What duties did Mr. Kubura perform at the time?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there he was the Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when Mr. Kubura became the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of August 1993. I remember that event because that was the time when I became the commander of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was located in Bilmiste you said. Where were the men from the 2nd Battalion trained?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Since that would involve my duties as the operations and training officer, all the training that took place at -- during that period of time took place in the Bilmiste barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, as a member of the 2nd Battalion, were you involved in military operations and activities at the beginning of June 1993? Were you involved in the operations carried out by the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you inform the Chamber of the activities concerned and could you inform them of the period concerned and the location?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In June, on the 8th of June, there was Operation Ovnak. On the 11th of June --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to June 1993. Allow me to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June there was the Ovnak operation, and on the 11th of June, the Kakanj operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you directly involved in the Ovnak operation?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your battalion directly involved in that operation?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued orders to you while you were in the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: While I was the officer for operations and training, I received orders from the battalion commander alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we have some documents that we would like to show this witness, could the usher show these documents to the witness?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, we've already had a look at these documents; we did so in the course of the proofing. Could you tell me what Ovnak operation was. When did it start and when did you become directly involved in the operation?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Operation Ovnak was an operation to open up the Ovnak pass, to link up the Zenica-Ovnak-Han Bila road, to establish a link between Zenica, Han Bila, and Travnik. Preparations for the operation were carried out I would say around the 5th of June, between the 5th and 6th of June. We deployed in certain sectors. Reconnaissance was completed on the 6th of June. On the 7th of June, we made an attempt to carry out our combat task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allow me to interrupt you. Let's take this in chronological order. You said that on the 5th and 6th of June there were preparations Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. for the operation. Who gave you the order, or rather your battalion the order to take part in the operation?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: As an officer for operations and training, this task was assigned to me by my battalion commander. My battalion commander was probably assigned this task, or rather received this task from his superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the document under tab number 2. P419 is the exhibit number. Do you recognise the document? This is an order to carry out an attack in which your battalion participated.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's an order to attack signed by my battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the order was received, how did the men and the units of the 2nd Battalion set off to carry out this combat task?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Buses deployed the members of the 2nd Battalion in the sector of the village of Pojske, which is in the vicinity of Vrselje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at document under tab number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Mr. President, this is a new document, dated the 5th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Podzic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with this document. This is a marching order for our battalion signed by my battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at item 2 of this marching order.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does item 2 say exactly?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: It says that certain means should be used for the march. It says that the march should be -- that the men should be transported to carry out the march by buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does -- did you actually carry out this order? Did you actually do what it says under item 2?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the battalion arrived in the Pojske or Vrselje sector. If you remember, can you tell us when you arrived there exactly, at what time of day?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Well, it was at night, early dawn, on the 6th of June. And upon arriving in the village of Pojske and Vrselje sector, the troops were provided with accommodation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What further orders did you then receive?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of June, 1993, officers from the battalion command and officers of the basic units, of the main units used meant to carry out reconnaissance in order to prepare for the task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the first combat start?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On the following day, on the 7th of June, there were attempts made to carry out our task, but they were not successful. So one might say that we engaged in combat on the 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Since the attack was a failure, we had a meeting in the battalion, a briefing. We reorganised our forces and decided to try to carry out our combat task one more time on the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 7th of June, where were the men of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The unit members were in the sectors in the collection areas. These areas that are somewhat removed from the lines; they aren't exposed to enemy activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, 1993, when did the fighting start?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The fighting for the 2nd Battalion started in the early morning hours on the 8th of June, in the Crni Vrh/Usice sector. The purpose of the fighting was to penetrate the enemy's lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to use a map, and with your leave we would like to show this witness a map so that he can explain what he has just been testifying about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, you mentioned the village of Pojske and the village of Vrselje a minute ago. So could you point to these locations on the map and could you use a felt tip to encircle these villages.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could mark the locations with numbers 1 and 2. You said that you penetrated the line and that you engaged in the direction of Crni Vrh. Could you point to the location of Crni Vrh and encircle that location. You also mentioned the village of Usice, if it's easier for you to find it.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I marked Crni Vrh with number 3, that's where the units started moving. Number 4 indicates Usice. That was where we first started fighting and where we penetrated the enemy's lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the Usice feature. What is Usice in fact?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: We could say that it's a hill in military terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are two combat activities on that day. When did that activity come to an end in that sector?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In the Crni Vrh and Usice sector, we breached the enemy line in the morning, but to carry out the entire task we had to remain engaged until the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then receive another order from your battalion commander? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon we established lines at the positions that we had reached to the south of the village of Brajkovici and below the road from Han Bila to Travnik. Our main task was to establish a new line and prepare to hand over the line to units of the second echelon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever pass through that road?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: As far as the Han Bila-Travnik road is concerned, no, I never crossed the road nor did the troops do that because that wasn't part of the task that we had been assigned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When conditions were established to hand the line over, what did the 2nd Battalion do and what happened to the 2nd Battalion men?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon on the 8th of June, members of the 2nd Battalion withdrew to the Pojske sector, which is where we had set out from, and the commander informed me that we had received a new task in a completely different area. We could say that it was in the Zenica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the members of the 2nd Battalion return to the village of Pojske as ordered?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: All the men from the 2nd Battalion returned to the village of Pojske. They had arrived there by the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the commander issued a new order to you. Who was the commander and what was the order?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Battalion ordered me to prepare to move rapidly and to redeploy the battalion so that they could engage in combat action in the Kakanj area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you yourself stay in the Ovnak area where all these activities had already come to an end?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I think that very same evening I already arrived in Kakanj, and I was preparing to carry out early morning reconnaissance for the task that had been assigned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under tab 3, could you have a look at document DK23 and tell me whether you are familiar with this document, and if so, what is the document?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with this document; it's a plan of commander's reconnaissance for the operation that I have just mentioned. That was the new task that we were assigned. And as you can see, we didn't have sufficient time really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers of the 2nd Battalion at the end of the fighting returned to the village of Pojske, as you said. What was the next task that members of the 2nd Battalion were assigned and what did they do?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The next task assigned to 2nd Battalion members was to prepare to rapidly redeploy from the village of Brajkovici sector and to go to a new area, the area of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the term "rapidly deploy," what does that mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The battalion had been engaged in combat for three days, and according to certain rules the men need 24 hours to rest. But we couldn't abide by these rules. So when the units were withdrawn from the Brajkovici area, we had to immediately prepare the unit to move. And that's what I mean when I say prepare the unit to move rapidly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that that unit had to leave that sector as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the men actually manage to redeploy rapidly?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. By the 9th, in the afternoon, the units were in the area of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that during this period of time while Mr. Patkovic was the battalion commander you were, one could say, the deputy commander of the battalion. At that time, while there was action in the Ovnak area, did you tell your battalion members -- or did you see that your battalion members entered houses and looted them?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I was actively involved in carrying out the battalion's combat task, and I did not notice any men or any units from the 2nd Battalion acting in a way that might be described as entering inhabited places and looting them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did members of the 2nd Battalion leave the Ovnak area and how did they travel to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In the same way that we had arrived there. The unit was taken there by bus. They were taken to the wider Kakanj area by bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that the unit was rapidly redeployed, was it possible for these soldiers during this period of time to leave and to go home to have a rest? Was it possible for them to spend any time outside the unit?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: It wasn't possible for us to grant them leave, not even in the Brajkovici [as interpreted] area. They were very tired. They were exhausted. So -- but we couldn't even think about granting them leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there's a mistake in the transcript. The witness said that it wasn't possible for the soldiers to have a rest in the Pojske area, and the transcript says "Brajkovici." I think it's page 58, line 21 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When exactly did the soldiers of the 2nd Battalion come to the Kakanj sector and where did they come?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The soldiers of the 2nd Battalion came to the broader sector of Kakanj, to the sector of Kakanj. I believe the village was Zagradje and they got there as early as the late afternoon of that day.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not actually hear the last word.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the document number 4 in this bundle of documents, DK24, the Defence exhibit. I'm just going to repeat the question I asked you earlier on because it did not enter the transcript. When the -- when was it exactly that the soldiers of the 2nd Battalion came to the sector of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of June in the late afternoon, the sector of the village Zagradje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document and can you tell us what it stands for?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This document is an order for attack for the aforementioned operation in the sector of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How soon after the carrying out of this military operation do the soldiers need to come, to arrive at that deployment area in which these combat operations are to take place?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On the basis of my experience and on the basis of some rules and regulations, it should be at least 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the village Zagradje. Can you take a look at this order for attack, item number 14. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: KM, it means the command post of the brigade in the area of the village Zagradje. Could you tell us where exactly this village is situated? Let me make it more specific. Is this village in the surroundings of Kakanj and how far is it from Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: This is a village which is indeed in the surroundings of Kakanj, the village called Zagradje. I believe it is about half an hour -- half an hour's drive away from Kakanj, perhaps even shorter than that. I have been to this village. That's where we prepared, where our units prepared for the carrying out of this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One more question with regard to this same document. Who signed this document and in what capacity, on the last page?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On the last page the document is signed by Mr. Amir Kubura as the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to look at the map on which you marked certain positions and certain places that you referred to, and could you please sign it and put today's date on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence would like to tender this map into evidence for the Defence of Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It is entered into evidence for the Defence of General Kubura, DK38. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this number is incorrect. I think it should be more than 40 according to our evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last number was 45. My legal assistant has just pointed it out to me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, and thank you to the Defence for pointing it out. Yes, indeed, it would be DK46. [In English] DK46. [Interpretation] I do apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we would like to deal with another topic with regard to the -- one of the counts of the indictment, perhaps this is a good time for a break. Perhaps we could have a somewhat shorter break if you think it might speed things up with regard to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we shall have a break now. It is 20 past 5.00, and we shall continue at a quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, I checked the transcript during the break and just in order to make things quite clear I'd like to ask you another question. Upon completing the operation of Ovnak, where did the soldiers of the 2nd Battalion go back to, where were they redeployed? I'm thinking in terms of the area of Ovnak; I'm not thinking of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Upon completing the operation, the soldiers went back to the deployment area, the village of Pojske.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, did you in the beginning of November of 1993 take part in the combat activities around the city of Vares with your battalion?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the battalion commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a commander of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat this question once again, since a different answer went into the transcript. So once again, did you by the beginning of November as a commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade participate in combat activities in the vicinity of the city of Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did participate in those activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the bundle of documents, number 6. The document dated the 6th of November, 1993, and can you tell us what it represents. Does it refer to the combat activities that you have just confirmed having participated in?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The document is dated the 3rd of November, not the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, it's DK43.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the order to attack, and I participated in this with my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 5, could you just look at the signature. Who signed this document and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: On page 5, it is signed by Mr. Amir Kubura, as the commander of this brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Podzic, when you received this order, could you tell the Trial Chamber when and in what way did you go to the sector of the city of Vares.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Upon receiving this order, on the 3rd of November, we redeployed and we moved from the Bilmiste barracks in the deployment area in the village of Strijezevo, the broader sector of Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the document number 5 in your folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, it's a new document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you recognised it?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. This is the marching order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at item 2 of this order and the part that says "transport shall be organised in a combined way." There it is.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I have looked at item 2, and on the basis of this order, with regard to my unit, the relevant transport would be by bus from the barracks in Bilmiste to the village of Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this order carried out in the way in which it is indicated here in the order dated the 1st of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: For the 2nd Battalion in line with the order, we went by bus from the barracks of Bilmiste to the village of Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to make use of a map very briefly, and if you allow me I would like the map to be placed on the ELMO and that -- in order to make it easier for us to follow the testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the map and indicate the village of Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. I've marked the village of Strijezevo. I've put the number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when you got to the village of Strijezevo?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: We got there as early as the 3rd of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What actual task did your battalion have, or rather what orders did you issue to the members of your battalion upon arrival to the village?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Upon arrival to the village, in line with the general task, my battalion was interested with the task to, on the 4th of November, carry out an attack in the general direction of Strijezevo, Majdan Zimije, the city of Vares, and to cover the main roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what direction was this attack supposed to take place according to this order?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The shortest possible route from the sector of Strijezevo to go down to the sector of Pajtov Han and to carry out along the road to the city of Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark with an arrow just to make things perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you carried out that task and at what time?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I myself and my battalion did carry out this task in line with the orders we have received, in line with the planned time-scale, as well as all the other tasks that followed on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any combat activities on the road to the city of Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: My formation, my battalion, was moving in a V formation, according to the NATO doctrine, two companies ahead and one in reserve. When we came to the road, on both right and left, I mean the terrain was rather Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. narrow, and the leading elements of the two companies which went ahead shot -- fired shots in the air. And they tried to uncover possible ambushes at the outskirts of the city. Such a formation and such a movement was maintained until we entered the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you get to the city of Vares itself?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I think it was at around 11.00, between 10.00 and 11.00 in the morning. And when entering the city, I met the UNPROFOR officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to this officer?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: We talked for about 10 to 15 minutes. It was an officer of about 40 years of age, medium height. He came in an armoured vehicle with two escorts, and he asked who the commanding officer of the unit was. I introduced myself, and he repeated his question. He said, Are you the commanding officer of this unit or of the checkpoint, because behind my unit, at the very entrance to the city, a checkpoint had already been in the process of being set up by the civilian police. I confirmed that I was indeed the commanding officer of the unit moving in the direction of the town. And initially I said that the leading elements were the two companies ahead and that they were firing shots in the air as a provocation; he recognised that. And in military jargon he replied that there was no need for such shots because there were no armed forces in town. I translated this request into an order of mine, and I ordered for these shots to be stopped. I would also like to point out that in one of the two companies that went ahead, 70 per cent of members were originally from that very town and the surroundings. And following this information that the HVO forces had withdrawn from the town, some of them also starting firing shots in the air, as a kind of celebration and joy. This was the first liberated city and those were their homes. I told him so, and we stopped those shots being fired after two or three minutes. He said that he would like to take that opportunity, in the course of that conversation we were having, to draw our attention to the fact that we had to act in a certain military way in relation to the civilians we were to encounter in town, and I replied that I can guarantee from my soldiers that they would act in line with military honour. And I said, I hope you made the same request to the HVO in the period of time that they spent in this city. I was impressed by his answer to the effect that he himself had lists with regard to the centre of town. He had lists of the non-Croat population, and he asked for the same sort of military honour and behaviour on the part of HVO in relation to those citizens. His two escorts had their arms pointed at me, and I asked him to ask them to stop. And he ordered them to do so, and they only obeyed his orders halfway. Thereupon we parted and I never met this person again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you enter the very city of Vares and did the soldiers of the 2nd Battalion enter Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In the V formation that I've mentioned before, the reserve company was stopped and it did not continue to move in the direction of the city. The two companies that had already entered the city -- well, one continued to move along the main road. They continued to move through the city itself in the direction of the buildings and the settlements of Dastansko and Przici. And the remaining third company started the manoeuvre of linking up with our forces to the right and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the situation in town when you entered?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Since the previous night the HVO and some inhabits withdrew from the city, it was fairly chaotic, probably due to this very rapid withdrawal and bad roads leading away from the town and the fact that people left at night. There were a lot of things scattered about, belongings, and coming out of the city there was a building built out of concrete and wood, and it was on fire. I could describe this situation as having arisen duly -- as having arisen partly intentionally and partly unintentionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay and how long did the soldiers that entered the city stay there?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: One company was -- the reserve company did not even enter, and the other marched through the town very quickly, and they came out in the northern part. And one company stayed to link up with the forces to the right and left. This activity lasted until perhaps 3.00 p.m. I moved along the main road and supervised the carrying out of this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did other units start coming to Vares, any other formations?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Right on the hills of my unit there was the civil police, and they set up a checkpoint whilst I was talking to the UNPROFOR officer. And that's why he asked me whether I was the commanding officer of that checkpoint or those forces. And about a quarter of an hour later, three other units appeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get an order whilst you were in Vares and what was that order?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: At around 3.00 p.m., when in the northern part of town I was establishing some sort of defence line with a unit in order to pre-empt any surprises and we were trying to link up with our forces to the right and left, at that stage I received an order to organise my forces, carry out controls, and to leave the town with the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued that order?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I received the order from the commander of the brigade, Mr. Kubura; it was in a written form and it was forwarded to other officers in both oral and written form. And thereupon, we organised our forces and led the 2nd Battalion out of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your battalion follow the orders, your orders I mean, and did they leave?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I've organised my units fully, and I issued some additional oral orders specifying the place where they had to gather. It was a square in the city, a rather large square. And soldiers had to have their soldier's kits with them, only exclusively, their rifles, their rucksacks, their ammunition. And they had to move through the checkpoint in a column. I mean the checkpoint that I had mentioned being set up. At that checkpoint, there was the combined civilian and military police. To the left, if we think in terms of the way out of town, there was the deputy of the brigade commander and one officer from the 3rd Corps command, and two representatives of the civilian authorities who were watching my unit and my battalion as they went past and they went through that checkpoint. I think that the deputy commander, the brigade deputy commander, on the basis of random sample singled out two soldiers and asked me to check their rucksacks. We found nothing in those rucksacks. And as they went through the checkpoint, the soldiers were allowed to carry only their soldier equipment and kits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the deputy commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brzina, Halil. He was to the left and controlled any movement that was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you have a look at the document under tab number 7, please. Do you recognise the person who drafted the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, Mr. President, this is a new document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Podzic, who was this combat report forwarded to, addressed to?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: This is a combat report addressed to the command of the 3rd Corps, and it's from the assistant Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade, Mr. Zunic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this report reflect what you have just been testifying about?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it does, and it was drafted on the basis of our reports once these tasks had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at document under tab number 8, under tab number 9, the document under tab number 9 is a new document and the same is the case -- or rather, number 9 is -- number 8 is a new document and number 9 is P478.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order -- or these orders, since we have two documents here. And after the town was left, an order was issued forbidding unit members to enter and stay in the house. It also mentions the penalties that will be imposed on anyone who violates the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Podzic, did members of your battalion loot the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Members of my battalion participated in the liberation of the town of Vares, and they did not do anything that could be described as theft, let alone looting. I think that when we left this town in an organised manner, we did so in a highly professional and disciplined way. And individuals from various fields witnessed this fact, two levels of command, brigade command, the command of the corps. There were representatives of the civilian authorities and some civilians who witnessed this fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at document under tab 10; it's a new document. Could you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this document. This document is a scroll of honour for our brigade, or rather for the unit that I was a member of, and it is for the extraordinary contribution and for the maintenance of the continuity of authority. It was signed by the then-head of the municipality, Mrs. Mervana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the date?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The date is the 18th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Podzic. This concludes our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to ask the witness to sign the map, and then we would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution with regard to the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I note that there are no comments. Mr. Registrar, but no mistakes this time, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number is DK47. This is the exhibit number for Mr. Kubura's Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We do have some questions. I'm not sure if we will be able to finish this evening, but I will commence if the Chamber would like me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Podzic. My name is Daryl Mundis and along with my colleagues here we represent the Prosecution in this case. I do have some questions for you, sir, but before I do that I would like to simply let you know that it is not in any way our intention to confuse you with any of your questions. And I would ask you, sir, if you don't understand any of my questions, simply to tell me that and I will rephrase or repeat the question so that you understand it. Is that clear, sir?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Good evening. Yes, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me start, sir, by asking you a couple of additional questions about Vares, since that's where we ended, or the Defence for Brigadier Kubura ended. You've mentioned a couple of times that there was a person from the 3rd Corps command, and I'm wondering if you can recall precisely who it was from the 3rd Corps who was present in Vares in November at the time this campaign was undertaken?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I can't remember who that person was, but he was certainly from the corps command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what position this person had within the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall at the time you entered Vares whether you were aware at that point in time that the HVO had already withdrawn from the city of Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No. That was why I said that we opened fire -- we fired in the air in provocation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- just that we're then clear, sir, the first time you became aware that the HVO had in fact previously withdrawn from Vares was when the UNPROFOR officer informed you of that. Is that -- is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR officer met me at the entrance to the town, and he said that it wasn't necessary to open fire since there were certainly no more HVO members in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, just so we're clear, that was the first time that you became aware that the HVO had previously withdrawn from Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: That was the first time that I was informed that all of the men had withdrawn from Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember, sir, or can you be more precise as to what the UNPROFOR officer told you as to when the HVO had withdrawn from Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he didn't say when. He had the bearing of a member of the military. He immediately warned us to stop firing in the air and assured us that all members of the HVO had left Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you don't remember if he told you they -- the HVO left earlier this morning or the HVO left yesterday or the HVO left two days ago? You don't remember him specifically telling you when the HVO had withdrawn from Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember him telling me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, I assume, but I would just like you to verify or correct me if I'm wrong, but I assume since you told us that no members of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade were in any way involved in theft or looting, it would follow then that no one from the 2nd Brigade -- or 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was arrested or disciplined or prosecuted for any acts of theft or looting in Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I have already testified and confirmed that we had left the town in an organised manner. We hadn't taken any property from the town, and I confirm that at that point in time none of the soldiers had anything that wasn't military equipment. But I did not say that no one was processed before and afterwards, not only from this unit but from other units, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, sir, in order that we're all clear, are you telling us that no soldiers from any unit of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was arrested or disciplined or prosecuted for the crime of theft or looting in the city of Vares during the campaign in November -- early November 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that in the course of the operation on the 4th, when leaving the town no men from the 2nd Battalion engaged in looting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. My question is related but is slightly different. My question is: Were you aware, as the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, whether any of the soldiers in your battalion were ever arrested, disciplined, or prosecuted for the offence of theft or looting concerning the events that occurred or the campaign that occurred in the city of Vares in the first week of November 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the one concrete and wood building that you told us about that was on fire, did you observe any other destruction of buildings or houses or any other structures in the city of Vares after the arrival of your battalion in that city?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I've already said that the situation in the town was fairly chaotic, and I even expanded on this in a certain manner and said that this was probably caused by the HVO's withdrawal. To a certain extent, that was probably intentional. What I noticed was the building on fire in northern part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note for the transcript there needs to be a correction on page 75, line 12, the witness's answer was "I don't remember." And the following sentence is actually the next question, that is "other than the one concrete and wood building," is the next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you again, sir, if you were aware or had knowledge of whether any soldiers in the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade were ever arrested or disciplined or prosecuted for any crimes involving unlawful destruction of buildings or arson or torching buildings or any offences related to property in the sense of buildings or structures in the city of Vares?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn briefly to the situation in the Ovnak area in June of 1993. You told us earlier, sir, as reflected on page 58, line 10 of the transcript, that there was no looting by soldiers of your battalion, the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, in the Ovnak area. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I know, Witness, that at that point in time you were not the battalion commander but were rather the operations and training officer for that battalion. But were you aware with respect to the events in the Ovnak area in June whether any soldiers of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade were ever arrested, disciplined, or prosecuted for the crimes of looting or theft with respect to events that took place in Ovnak in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe at any point in time while your unit was in the immediate vicinity of Ovnak whether any soldiers of your battalion were engaged in any unlawful destruction of property, again to include lighting -- intentionally lighting buildings on fire or intentionally in any way destroying property in the form of buildings, houses, sheds, barns, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No, I never noticed anything of that kind. And given the way the unit was used, the unit advanced very rapidly so I can't see how someone could have found the time to engage in such activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that this operation was being undertaken, did you observe any buildings, houses, barns, or sheds that were on fire?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I did not notice any buildings on fire, but before the beginning of the operation the first defence line of the HVO was at the limit, at the outskirts, of an inhabited place. And they had previously had certain buildings that were damaged. That was at the entrance to Ovnak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But again, at the time that you were there with the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, you did not observe any buildings on fire?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of any soldiers of your battalion being prosecuted, arrested, or disciplined in any way for any types of offences against property in the Ovnak area with respect to events in June of 1993? And again, I'm referring to torching of buildings, arson, or any other kind of unlawful destruction of property in the Ovnak area.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, and also because I was the -- an officer in the staff, I don't remember such a case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn now, sir, to the issue of training, and I understand that you were responsible for training in the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade from mid-March 1993 until August 1993, when you assumed command of that battalion. You told us earlier - again reflected on page 51, line 8, of the transcript - that the training took place -- the training for your battalion took place in the Bilmiste barracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any locations outside of the barracks where soldiers of the 2nd Battalion, 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade underwent training?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any point in time, sir, while you were the trainings and ops officer for the battalion, were soldiers from your battalion trained by foreigners?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: From the time that I arrived in the 7th Brigade and from the time that I assumed my duties in the battalion and onwards, no, that never occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become aware at any point in time whether foreigners were involved in training the battalion or its members prior to the time that you joined the battalion?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us -- or in response to a question from the Defence, that the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was Asim Koricic, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and he was the commander until the beginning of August 1993, and this is reflected on page 50, line 19. My question to you, sir, is: From the time period when you first joined the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in mid-March 1993, did you ever see Asim Koricic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him. I think that was in the beginning of April -- at the beginning of April in Visoko. He was the brigade commander in the village of Srhinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, sir, this would be April 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior -- was this is only occasion that you saw him during 1993 or did you see him on other occasions in 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Soon after that event, I'm not sure when that occurred, it was at the beginning of April though, but he went abroad. That's the information I had, and I believe that he arrived at the end of September or the beginning of October 1993. And on that occasion, I saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know where he went abroad and for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Apart from knowing that he had gone abroad, I did not know where he was nor did I know why he had gone abroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or did you hear any discussions at any meetings that you attended whether he had authority from the corps commander to be abroad, or did he just simply disappear and go abroad?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Since at the time I was a member of the battalion staff, all the meetings I attended were held in the battalion; they concerned the tasks to be carried out within the battalion. I didn't have access to any information that did not concern the battalion, so the sort of information on the authority that various individuals had was not the kind of information I had access to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to the best of your recollection and knowledge, following the period after Mr. Koricic went abroad until the period at the beginning of August 1993 when Amir Kubura was formally appointed as the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, who was in command of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I was an officer for operations and training in the battalion, and it was the battalion commander who assigned tasks to me. The battalion commander would be assigned tasks by the brigade commander, and I could not provide you with any information as to other elements within the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically you don't know the answer to the question that I just put to you. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see my learned friend -- excuse me, sir, but I see my colleague on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise for interrupting you, but I think there's a mistake in the transcript. The witness said that the command battalion received an order from the brigade command, not from the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The battalion and the battalion commander received tasks from the brigade commander, and I received tasks from the battalion commander. But I had no responsibility for the sort of tasks that were issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So again --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I thank my colleague for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me again ask you the question. It seems to me based on your answers, then, you weren't in the position to know who was exercising the command functions for the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, in light of the fact that your own orders were being directly given to you by the 2nd Battalion commander. Is that a fair summary of the situation, sir?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: A correct summary would be to say that a subordinate officer has the duty to know his immediate superior. In that -- in my case, it was the battalion commander. He would receive orders. And as to how orders were issued at other levels, I really couldn't say. It really wasn't for me to show interest in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let me ask you: Do you still have the bundle of documents that the Defence gave you or ... Could you please turn to tab 1, the first document -- could you please turn to tab 1, the first document. And I'm wondering, sir, if you can help us out with respect to the addressees or the units to which this document was delivered. I see down towards the bottom it says "commander of Polo." Can you tell us what that is? Do you have any idea or any knowledge what Polo, P-o-l-o, refers to?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that this abbreviation means anti-armour rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in June of 1993 had some kind of anti-armour rocket launcher unit. Would that -- is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we had a number of units that were in a state of readiness, and they were manned but they didn't have the adequate type of weapons that such a unit should have had. The brigade, or rather the unit had to be organised as it should have been organised in accordance with the establishment rules, although it didn't have adequate weapons. But I don't think that we had such weapons systems at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the unit that's listed immediately above that on the addressee list. It says "one times commander of guerrilla group." Do you know what that's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Within the 2nd Battalion there were two anti-sabotage platoons, which in 1993 were called guerrilla units. But at the beginning of 1994, they were transferred into reconnaissance and sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these two anti-sabotage platoons, which in 1993 were known as guerrilla units, have any names?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: One was called Planina, mountain, and the other town, or rather Grad. Mountain was supposed to be used in mountainous terrain, and town, the unit town was to be used for combat in towns and in inhabited places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, these two guerrilla units, the Planina and the Grad, or the mountain and the town guerrillas, these two units remained within the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade throughout 1993 and into 1994?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: In 1993 we had these two platoons and in the course of 1994 as well. They sustained terrible losses. I think that at least 30 to 40 per cent of them were killed. I know almost all the members of these units; they were wounded on two or three occasions. Sometime in the course of 1994 one group was formed of the men that remained from these two groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, these two units, were they considered in effect to be elite units?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: These two units were prepared and used to carry out extremely complex tasks, for example, infiltration, destroying very strong points of resistance. And given the purpose, they were more noticeable, they stood out, in the battalion. I would also like to add that the name "guerrilla" was frequently used, and it is still used to this very day in many countries where war is waged in such a manner that attacks are carried out in this manner without any artillery support, attacks against very strong points of resistance, against artillery strongholds, et cetera. This is a manner of fighting that is the reason for which units have this name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The witness did not mention anti-sabotage units, just a sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these two units, sir, based in any particular place during 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: These two units were part of the 2nd Battalion. They were billeted in the Bilmiste barracks in the same building where the battalion command was located, on the floor above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, who was responsible for the training of these two units? Did that also fall within your responsibility, or was there a special training regime that these units underwent in light of their purpose and the missions that were entrusted to them?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: These two units were directly linked to the battalion commander, and every unit commander is directly accountable and responsible for the training of his soldiers, so the commander was responsible for their training. Of course, as an operations and training officer, I did develop training plans. And within the framework of the training of this unit -- well, their training was somewhat more complex if we compare it to the infantry troops, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, other than -- other than the two guerrilla unit that you've just told us about, were you aware of any other units within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade during 1993 that also used the term "guerrilla" as a descriptive term for their unit?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've never heard of a unit called the Plavi Sokol or Blue Falcons Guerrilla Unit?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: One of these units that we have been talking about is precisely that unit, guerrilla Grad, town, was basically the Blue Falcon Platoon, Plavi Sokol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard or were you aware in 1993 of a unit known as the Turkish guerrilla?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I had heard of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard, sir, in relation to that unit that it had formally formed part of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or that it was part of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: At the time when I arrived at that unit, it wasn't an integral part of that brigade. It wasn't later as far as I know on the basis of conversations I had with other people. It had not been a part of it before either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you had heard with respect to this unit?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Very briefly and roughly, I heard that in the Zenica sector there was the so-called Turkish guerrilla and that it was somewhere at the outskirts of town. Considering the dynamics of the use and the task of the unit that I belonged to, it is quite logical that I had no more specific information, not only with regard to this unit but many other units as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have three questions only and it won't take long. Further examination by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Podzic, my learned colleague has shown you number 1 in the folder. Could you simply read out the preamble to this document, the marching order.

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: "In the spirit of the upcoming task and in accordance with the order of the 7th Muslim Brigade" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The command or the commander?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The command of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question: You said that you knew most members of the unit that was stamped guerrilla units. Who were members of those units?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I can actually state with a great degree of certainty. I know all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Were they all Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: They were all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina; they were all Bosniaks, and they were all people who had been born and were living in either Zenica or in the surrounding sectors. I could even tell you what villages they came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, Mr. President. Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I would like to put you one or two questions on your stay in Vares. You said you entered Vares in the morning at 10.00 or 11.00 and you had a conversation with UNPROFOR officer. And you said also about a quarter of an hour after that conversation other -- three other units appeared. Could you tell us what kind of units that they were?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was engaged in that conversation. As I said, it lasted for about 15 minutes, or rather about a quarter of an hour after we entered, several other units showed up and they were units of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I can assume this -- I mean, it is beyond my level, but I believe that they were units from the 1st Corps of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And in terms of the operational level, their task was to take over the lines that we had established and to set up a new line which had been somewhat damaged in the area of responsibility of that operations group, to position the reserve forces, and to set up a checkpoint. Certainly we are talking about two different units and the police force that set up the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I suppose they came from the north, is that right, and you came from the south?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: No. Those units were behind my units, perhaps 15 minutes behind us. As far as I can remember, in terms of the general idea, to the north there were the members of the 2nd Corps and I believe that they, too, entered from the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You also said that two of your units crossed the town quickly, and the third unit tried to link up with other units in the field. Now, you said that: "3.00 I was trying to establish some defence line in the northern part of the city, then I got an order to leave Vares." Between 2.00 and 11.00 in the morning and 3.00 in afternoon, where were you yourself?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Allow me to say by way of introduction that one of the reserve units did not enter the city at all, and the two units that were at the front of the battalion entered the city. One continued to the north in the direction of Dastansko and Przici, and one started linking up with the forces to the right and left in town. So this is what I've had already explained. I had also mentioned before that after we directed the unit to the northern part of town, in the direction of Dastansko and Przici, and after we started linking up with the other forces, we also controlled the road from the south to the north of town, from one unit to the other, and that's of course the duty of the commander and the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: When you got the order to leave Vares, I understand that you were at the northern part of the town where your two units were, but maybe I'm mistaken. And supposing this to be the case, in what direction did you leave the town? Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: I said that I received orders to withdraw the battalion from the city, and I received a whole series of oral instructions as well, one of which was with regard to the southern part of town. I was meant to concentrate all my forces, two companies that is, in that part of town, to gather my forces that is, and to take them out through the checkpoint in the south of the city, in the direction of our initial deployment sector, that is to say, the village of Strijezevo. So we marched to -- out of town to the south in the direction of the village Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And when marching through Vares to the south, to the village Strijezevo, did you notice anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: The main characteristics I would like to stress in the course of this march, that is to say, we went through the checkpoint and I've described the way it was done, who was present, as well as the movement of the other units. And the forces from probably the police and the 1st Corps they were moving and ended in the direction of the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
