utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one question only; it's going to be very quick, and we are going to try and conclude today. You referred to the mountain guerrillas. One witness we had some time ago who was a member of the military police within the 3rd Corps had explained to us that the mountain guerrillas belonged to the 7th Brigade and that there was a kind of inquiry carried out with regard to them and due to the fact that they engaged in illegal behaviour. Do you have any recollection of such an investigation with regard to this so-called mountain guerrilla?

utterances.speaker: KASIM PODZIC
utterances.text: Since all investigations and inquiries are carried out under a veil of secrecy, I had no information of any units or individuals from this battalion being the subject of such an inquiry or any investigation. But on the basis of individual accountability and responsibility, there were indeed members. I do remember the fact that some members of the unit were actually put on trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Commander, for having come to testify here in The Hague. Your hearing has finished, and I'd like to wish you all the best and a safe return home and all the best in your work. I would like to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom. In a couple of minutes -- and I'm turning to the Defence team for General Kubura, there will be no hearing next week. Could you announce the programme for the week after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, two things: What documents would you like to tender, and then the programme?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. There will be some work for the registrar. We've got the document number 1 on our list, the marching order of the 5th of June, 1993; the document number 5 on the list, dated the 1st of November, 1993; and the document number 7, the 4th of November, 1993; and number 8, dated the 5th of November, 1993; and number 10, dated the 18th of March, 1994. I can tell you straight ahead so as not to waste any more time, we know that we are not having any hearings next week, and by the beginning of next week at the latest we'll be submitting the list of witnesses that we'll be calling before this Court after the break. For the week after the break, we'll presumably have four witnesses for the first four days of hearing, as we had agreed previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. So we shall start again on Monday, the 2nd of May, at 2.15. Is that so, registrar? You had the list of hearings earlier. It is Monday, the 2nd of May. So out of these five documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five numbers in English very quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In English and with no mistakes I hope. [In English] The 5th of June, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK48, with an English version DK48/E; the second document dated 1st of November, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK49, with an English version DK49/E; the third document dated 4th of November, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK50, with an English translation DK50/E; the document dated 5th of November, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK51, with an English translation DK51/E; and finally, the document dated 18th of March, 1994, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK52, with an English translation DK52/E. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no other items outstanding, no questions, no questions from the Prosecution either. In that case, I apologise to the interpreters for having worked ten minutes longer, but we won't have a hearing tomorrow after all. So do please come back on the 2nd of May, on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of May, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
